stem: Triangle \(PQR\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. What is the area of triangle \(PQR\)?
solution: \(P\) and \(Q\) have the same \(y\)-coordinate, so \(\overline{PQ}\) is horizontal with length \(6 - (-2) = 8\).
The height is the vertical distance from \(R\) to \(\overline{PQ}\): \(7 - 1 = 6\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1}{2}(8)(7)\); it uses the \(y\)-coordinate of \(R\) as the height instead of the distance \(7 - 1 = 6\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(8 \cdot 6\); it leaves out the \(\frac{1}{2}\) in the triangle area formula.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1}{2}(8)(8)\); the height was found as \(7 + 1\) instead of \(7 - 1\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
pts={p['label'][0]:(p['x'],p['y']) for p in figure['points']}
P,Q,R=pts['P'],pts['Q'],pts['R']
ans=Rational(1,2)*abs((Q[0]-P[0])*(R[1]-P[1])-(R[0]-P[0])*(Q[1]-P[1]))
assert ans==24
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
